key_insight: Among several HVOF-sprayed cermet coatings on 65G steel, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall balance of density, hardness, and low friction.
engineering_relevance: For abrasive-adhesive wear applications in machinery, power, and metallurgy, the powder composition and binder phase strongly control coating performance.
method: HVOF deposition of WC–Co–Cr, WC–NiCr, WC–Ni, Cr3C2–NiCr, and Al2O3–NiCr coatings onto 65G steel.
Characterization by SEM/EDS plus microhardness, roughness, tribology, and adhesive/scratch testing.
Comparison of microstructure–property relationships across cermet systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative performance differences, including WC–Co–Cr with the lowest friction coefficient (0.143) and highest microhardness (1316.87 HV), while Al2O3–NiCr showed the highest friction (0.630) and lowest hardness (631.59 HV).
watch_item: Surface roughness varied widely (Ra = 3.881–8.130 μm), so coating performance will still depend on spray conditions and process control.
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF THE COMPOSITION OF METAL-CERAMIC POWDERS ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE PROPERTIES OF COATINGS OBTAINED BY THE HVOF METHOD
